name: Alexander Nanta Linggi
_note: M2 cohort: federal cabinet minister, Works portfolio continuous since 3 Dec 2022 (additionally assigned Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives in Dec 2025). Data on file; below ranking validity pending further objective dimensions and the Layer B panel. metrics.justification: No corruption charge or conviction of record. A review of court and anti-corruption records to the source date found no personal matter against the minister. Recorded as the subject's own factual status only.

metrics.justification: Crisis response in the Works remit after the 18 Nov 2025 ECRL steel-canopy collapse onto the MRR2: within days CIDB opened a probe under s.34C of the Construction Industry Development Act 1994 and a stop-work order was issued to the developer, with a parallel DOSH safety probe. Fast, named statutory instrument; resolution measurability pending the final report (anchor 3).

citation.title: CIDB launches probe into ECRL steel canopy collapse on MRR2, works halted

metrics.justification: Barrier-free Multi-Lane Free Flow tolling, championed for 2024 rollout, slipped repeatedly and by 23 Jan 2025 was still being "refined" and not operative; the National Slope Master Plan (launched 2025) was not confirmed gazetted. Reform championed but materially delayed/diluted (anchor 2).

citation.title: MLFF to be refined further to ensure safety, efficiency, views of industry players sought – works minister

metrics.justification: On 9 Dec 2025 the Works Ministry formed a special committee to monitor "sick" (critically delayed) projects and tighten enforcement against contractors, following a PM directive. A new internal mechanism, but reactive and secretary-general-led rather than a documented strengthening of an independent institution (anchor 2).

citation.title: Works Ministry sets up special committee to act on 'sick' projects

metrics.justification: On 3 Feb 2026 he addressed and explained a controversial "if you don't like us, just divorce us" podcast remark on the record, clarifying it was a spontaneous allusion and not a call for Sarawak to separate, rather than denying he said it. A clarification of a remark, not a policy reversal (anchor 2).

citation.title: I didn't mean Sarawak wants to split from Malaysia, says Nanta
